annotations.annotation_text: Fall/resurrection motif "Wall" on page 496 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Tim Finnegan tumbling from his ladder, Humpty Dumpty shattering from the wall, Adam falling in Eden — all converge within the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. The comic-cosmic Fall during the Age of Men phase demands its counterpart: resurrection through the whiskey-splash of the water of life (uisce beatha).
sources: The Ballad of Tim Finnegan's Wake. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan%27s_Wake
Atherton, James S. The Books at the Wake. https://archive.org/details/booksatwake0000athe
Opie, Iona and Peter. The Oxford Dictionary of Nursery Rhymes. https://archive.org/details/oxforddictionary0000unse_m4u1

annotations.annotation_text: Liturgical echo "Pater" on page 496 ("The Inquest of Yawn"): Catholic ritual, Latin prayer, and sacramental language weave through the judicial inquest over the prostrate body of Yawn (Shaun), voices of the dead rising through him, HCE's final confession. Joyce fuses ecclesiastical solemnity with domestic banality during the Age of Men phase, treating the tavern counter as communion rail and the sleeping body as sacred vessel.
sources: Contemporary Literature Press: Classical Lexicon for FW. https://editura.mttlc.ro
Frazer, Sir James George. Folk-Lore in the Old Testament. https://archive.org/details/folkloreinoldtes01frazuoft
